coverage_note: Whole file read. Mostly a nature-vocab and grammar Q&A lesson; long English meta stretches (09:55-11:30 on دير بال, 55:20-1:02:30 on المفضل عندي, 1:04:11-end app talk). Self-fixes not written: 06:51 قلقان->قلقانين, 30:29 ثلاث مرة->مرات, 50:27 حجور/حجرات->حجار, 22:03 قمر->القمر. Pronunciation (S4) not written: 15:37 قلات=غلطات, 30:11 maratat, 36:45 تلجات (Amal تَلَّجَت; he said تلجت right at 35:25). Repeats not scored: 04:07, 21:46, 44:20. 29:41 بمطر? and 34:15 بتلج? are questions. 06:10 'dangerous' not on her sheet, so not tier 3. Echo candidates all real English (no echo fixes). laazem_noun 12:56 is a meta question, not a B2 slip. Engine garble: 02:23 لسة الخطيب بتاع = Amal's recast عيانة; 32:14 زعلتكش عن = her عن; 47:24 وحدات = وردات?; 21:09 شجرة متيارة.

rows.why: He described his fiancée (feminine) with the masculine adjective; Amal recast it as عيانة.
Said masculine عيان again for خطيبتي after her 02:00 fix; she said عيانة again and he took it ('Yeah, عيانة').
rows.english: My fiancée is a bit sick.

rows.why: He made the person the subject of بيوجع and tacked راسها on after; Amal recast with راسها before the verb; 04:07 is a repeat.

rows.medi_said: I don't know how to say cough. She has a cough.
rows.amal_said: They say but كح. I say كحة.
rows.why: He said he did not know 'cough'; Amal supplied كحة.

rows.medi_said: الـ or لا الـ نار. / لـ النار for fire
rows.amal_said: Men not. ... You're worried about. You're worried from. ... Men، men.
rows.why: قلقان takes من; he used لـ and Amal gave من (he took it: 'We would say من, right?').

rows.amal_said: no. There's another word for that.
rows.right: (another verb for a fire starting, not supplied)
rows.why: He used يبدأ (begin) for a fire starting; Amal said no, there is another word, and set it aside.

rows.medi_said: do I know how to say taking care or like caring for?
rows.why: He asked how to say 'take care of'; Amal supplied ديرت بالي.
دير بال needs على before the person; he left it out and Amal recast with على (while still teaching the phrase).
rows.english: I took care of my fiancée.

rows.why: Same missing على after her 09:51 recast; Amal named it: 'بدير بالي takes على'.
rows.english: I took care of my fiancée.

rows.amal_said: دير بالك is actually the command form.
rows.why: His second example came out as a garbled command; Amal said the command form is دير بالك. Unclear what he meant.
After خلينا the next verb is a bare present (نعمل), not past عملنا; Amal recast and he repeated.

rows.medi_said: الدرس إنه، uh, إنه تخطط-- uh, تفتتلي.
rows.why: He meant 'the lesson that you planned' and used إنه + present instead of اللي + past; Amal only said كيف يعني and moved on (my reading of the right form).
rows.english: Let's do the lesson that you planned.

rows.medi_said: Uh, عصا- is it، أسف؟ ... is it عصافير؟ ... أنا نسيته.
rows.why: He forgot 'sky' (said أنا نسيته); Amal rejected عصافير and supplied سما.
Listing what is in the sky he used singular غيم; Amal asked 'one?' and he switched to plural غيوم.

rows.medi_said: When, when do you look at the sky? When do you watch the sky?
rows.amal_said: No، امتى بتتطلع على الشمس would be when do you watch the sky؟ امتى الشمس بتطلع؟
rows.wrong: When do you watch the sky?
rows.right: When does the sun rise (امتى الشمس بتطلع)
rows.why: He heard her بتطلع (rise) as بتتطلع (look); she said no and explained.

rows.medi_said: أنا نسيت الكلمة بس سجر. سجر؟
rows.why: He produced a non-word سجر for فجر (dawn), a word from an early lesson; Amal said فجر.
He added لو to غير for 'other than'; Amal said 'No لو. غير.'

rows.medi_said: الشمس و و يوم شو، شو في.
rows.why: The phrase is غير + bare noun (no el-); he said الشمس and Amal recast غير شمس و يوم; he then asked about the el-.
rows.english: Other than the sun and the day, what is there?

rows.why: For 'the sky at night' he put night first and sky last with no el-; Amal recast السما بالليل.
Amal asked how to say dark; he forgot and she supplied عتمة.
'One' goes after the noun (شمس وحدة); Amal accepted it, only echoing واحدة (my reading).
After the noun تاني agrees: نجمة تانية; Amal echoed تاني and he fixed to تانية, she said مهم.
The verb in the relative clause needs the pointer back to نجمة; Amal prompted and he said بشوفها ('I forgot the pointer rule').
rows.english: This is the first star I see today.

rows.medi_said: since is لسـ-- لسا, right? ... Is it لا؟
rows.amal_said: No. Since-- لا is until. ... من.
rows.why: He did not know 'since', guessed لسا then لا; Amal said no and supplied من.
He said الأول (the first) for الهوا; Amal recast and, when he asked what he said, repeated الأول.
For 'different' he said بعيد (far); Amal asked for the word and he ended with غير عن at 32:47. Sheet: 'different (from) | mu5talef | مختلف'.
rows.english: The air here is different from the air there.

rows.medi_said: بعيد من cuz it's comparative, right?
rows.why: He chose من; Amal gave عن (engine garbled the rest) and he asked 'always takes عن?' and used it.

rows.amal_said: آخر المرة means the last of the time. The end of the time. ... آخر مرة. The last time.
rows.why: آخر + el- means 'the end of'; 'the last time' is آخر مرة, Amal explained.
The subject مرة is feminine so the verb is كانت; Amal prompted 'مرة is' and he said كانت.
rows.english: (The last time) was three years ago.

rows.amal_said: No. ثلاث سنين الماضيين ... would be for the last three years. Ago is قبل. So قبل ثلاث سنين.
rows.why: He used الماضي (past) for 'ago'; Amal said no, 'ago' is قبل.
He said سنان (teeth) for سنين (years) right after she gave سنين; she asked 'What's سنان?' and he said teeth, then years.

rows.amal_said: إيش يعني عجل؟ ... عجا كتير الصباح؟ إيش يعني؟
rows.why: الهوا is singular so the verb is أجا, not plural أجو; Amal echoed it as عجا (singular) before he said 'it's singular. Aja'.
rows.english: The wind came a lot this morning.

rows.amal_said: Tell me it was very strong. The wind was very strong in the mornings.
rows.why: 'Came a lot' is not how the wind is described; Amal did not understand and gave the English for 'was very strong'; he said الهوا كان قوي كتير.
rows.english: The wind was very strong this morning.

rows.medi_said: الهوا أجو كتير الصباح / الهوا كان قوي كتير الصباح
rows.why: 'In the morning' needs بـ or الصبح (she used الصبح بكير at 18:50); he said bare الصباح and Amal let it pass (my reading).
The object الأرض needs the ending on the verb; Amal prompted 'It.' and he said نظفتها.
Listing things on the land he said singular الوردة; Amal queried (engine: وحدات) and he switched to plural وردات, she said Mm.

rows.medi_said: Is it the bee? Is it bee plants?
rows.why: He could not find 'plants'; Amal supplied زريعة.
He offered رمل for dirt/soil; Amal said it is sand, and he then found تراب.

rows.medi_said: I don't, أنا بعرف، ما بعرف.
rows.why: He forgot 'stones'; Amal supplied حجر.
He meant the old streets (plural, قديمة); Amal recast الشوارع.
The adjective after the definite الشوارع takes el- too; Amal said الإدام.

rows.amal_said: Or just حجر. Are stone. ... Made of is different than made.
rows.why: He used مع (with) for 'made of'; Amal dropped the verb and preposition: الشوارع الإدام في أمريكا حجر.
rows.english: The old streets in America are made of stone.

rows.amal_said: تاني حجر or الحجر التاني. You said it first right.
rows.why: 'The second stone' is تاني حجر / الحجر التاني; حجر تاني means 'another stone'; Amal recast.

rows.amal_said: So you could either say my favorite stone or my favorite using عندي. المفضل عندي.
rows.proposed_rule: مفضل (favorite) is an adjective and never takes a possessive ending: say المفضل عندي or حجري المفضل, not مفضلي.
rows.why: He put the possessive ending on the adjective مفضل; Amal gave المفضل عندي and later said it 'never takes pronoun ending'.

rows.medi_said: I was gonna say الـ مفضل حجر.
rows.amal_said: الحجر المفضل or حجري المفضل. المفضل is an adjective.
rows.why: He put the adjective before the noun; Amal named it: المفضل is an adjective, so الحجر المفضل.
A noun with a possessive ending takes no el-; Amal: 'No ال first.'

rows.amal_said: But al-mufaddal is an adjective, so it follows ders. ... هاد الدرس المفضل عندي.
rows.why: After the definite الدرس the adjective takes el-: الدرس المفضل عندي; Amal named the rule.

rows.amal_said: مش هون. مش، مش في. مش هون. ... في is not is. في is there is.
rows.why: He used في as 'is' (isn't here); Amal: 'في is not is', say مش هون.
